diagnostic_evidence.quote: any continuous, piecewise smooth curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^d$ is a $(c\ell(\gamma)+1,c)$-approximate $t$-design curve on $S^d$ for any $c>0$

issues.failure_explanation: The definition bounds the error by ε|sup_{S^d}f|. For f∈P_t with sup f ≤ 0 (e.g. f = x₁−1) the right side is 0, so the definition demands exact identities generic curves do not satisfy: the paper's own observation that every curve is a (cℓ(γ)+1,c)-approximate t-design curve is false (f = x₁−1 forces c∫_γ(1−x₁) = 1 exactly); rmk:changec's step |∫_γ f| = ℓ(γ)|sup f| needs sup|f| ≠ |sup f|; and the displayed formula for ‖f‖_p in sub:norm/rmk:p is not the L^p norm. All proofs in fact bound with sup_{S^d}|f|, which is the evidently intended normalization; under the literal definition the approximate-design results do not hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |sup_{S^d}f| by sup_{S^d}|f| in Definition def:design, in the (ε,c,‖·‖*)-variant of Subsection sub:norm, and in rmk:p; the existing proofs then establish exactly the corrected statements.
issues.overall_effect: As literally written, the basic observations, lem:overlap/lem:smooth, rmk:changec/rmk:p/rmk:MZ, and the approximate-design theorems thm:const, thm:main, thm:even (and pro:caps's extension) are false or unproven, since functions with sup f ≤ 0 impose unmet exact constraints.
issues.title: Approximate-design error normalized by |sup f| instead of sup|f|
issues.why_classification: A one-token definitional correction, propagated mechanically, makes every proof go through with unchanged constants; no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a weighted $\lfloor t/2\rfloor$-design curve $\alpha=(\alpha_\Bbb R,\alpha_\Bbb C)$ on $S^2\subset\Bbb R\times\Bbb C$ satisfying $\alpha_\Bbb R(s)\neq-1$ for $s\in[0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: α₃ = −1 occurs exactly at midpoints s = (2j+1)/(4t) where α₁ = 0 and sin(πj/t + θ₁(0)) = −1, i.e. when θ₁(0) ≡ 3π/2 (mod π/t). The stated exclusion set {mπ − 2nπ/t} = {πk/t : k ∈ gcd(t,2)ℤ} is disjoint from the true forbidden set for odd t and strictly smaller for even t. Example: t = 1, θ₁(0) = π/2 satisfies the stated condition, yet α₃(s) = −1 at s = 3/4, where formula (3) is 0/0-undefined, violating thm:S3stitch's hypothesis α_ℝ ≠ −1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by the correct exclusion, e.g. θ₁(0) ≠ 3π/2 + mπ/t for all m ∈ ℤ (equivalently πj/t + θ₁(0) ≢ 3π/2 mod 2π for all j ∈ {0,…,2t−1}).
issues.overall_effect: For admissible θ₁ the d=3 curve of Theorem thm:weight is undefined at finitely many parameters, so the d=3 claim fails as stated (and some benign constant θ₁, e.g. 0, are needlessly excluded).
issues.title: Wrong exclusion condition on θ₁(0) in the d=3 part of thm:weight
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case fix: correcting the exclusion set (a routine trigonometric recomputation) preserves the method, conclusion, and scope of the d=3 construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: such a curve is given by the weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve

issues.failure_explanation: In eq:lift the base curve is cycled an integer number t'+1 of times, which is required both for closure (r(1) = r(0)) and for the design property (the fiber-Fourier selection needs an integer cycle count). In eq:explicitweight3 the cycle count is 4πt ∉ ℤ, so r(1) = {4πt} ≠ 0, the curve does not close, and it is not a weighted (4t−1)-design curve as claimed. The forced repair is r = 4ts − ⌊4ts⌋ (per thm:S3stitch with strength 4t−1) — or 8ts, which is what the claimed length corresponds to — a genuine choice of repair entangled with the length claim (ISSUE-004).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 4πt by an integer cycle count (4t, matching thm:S3stitch, or 8t, matching the length claim), noting that the length claim then needs the separate repair of ISSUE-004.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, formula (3) does not define a closed curve of the type studied, so the explicit d=3 witness in Theorem thm:weight is invalid as written.
issues.title: Non-integer cycle count 4πt in eq:explicitweight3
issues.why_classification: A local parametrization fix (changing one coefficient to an integer) restores closure and the design property; no global argument is affected, though the choice of constant interacts with ISSUE-004.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve $\gamma_{(\alpha_3,\alpha_2,\alpha_1),\theta_2}$ on $S^3$ of length greater than or equal to $2\pi\sqrt{32t^4-8t^2+1}$

issues.failure_explanation: Direct computation of the length of the d=3 curve with integer cycle count r = 4ts, θ₁ ≡ 0, θ₂ ≡ 0 gives |γ'|² = 4π² + 128/(1−z²) − 32π/√(1−z²), hence ℓ ≈ 14.3 for t = 1, far below the claimed bound 2π√(32t⁴−8t²+1) = 10π ≈ 31.4; in general the minimal length for constant θ₁ is √(H²+V²) with horizontal part H = 4πt² and an adjustable vertical winding. The claimed value equals √((8πt²)² + (2π(4t²−1))²), i.e. it corresponds to an 8t-cycle parametrization, inconsistent with thm:S3stitch; under that reading the lower bound is still violated (t = 2, θ₁ ≡ 0, θ₂ ≡ 0 gives ℓ ≈ 32.06π < 2π√481 ≈ 43.86π). With the formula as literally printed (ISSUE-003) the curve is not closed and equality is unattainable. The bound/equality is thus incorrect under every consistent reading.

failure_location.quote: for $d=3$ and $C\geq2\pi\sqrt{32t^4-8t^2+1}$ (with equality when $\theta_1$ is constant for some $\theta_2$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the length of the corrected curve (H = 4πt² per 4t cycles plus adjustable vertical winding) and restate the bound and equality claim accordingly, keeping the existential claim 'for any C above the corrected bound' since length can be increased via θ₂ windings.
issues.overall_effect: The stated quantitative length guarantee for the d=3 weighted design curves (both the lower bound and the attainable equality) is unreliable; the qualitative existence and the order t² of the length are unaffected.
issues.title: Incorrect length bound for the d=3 weighted design curve
issues.why_classification: The specific quantitative guarantee is false and requires a real recomputation (a contained horizontal/vertical decomposition argument) and restatement, but the existence result and the asymptotic order survive with a comparable bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The pair $(X,\lambda:X\to\Bbb R)$ is called a \emph{weighted $t$-design set}

issues.failure_explanation: As printed, on the piece s ∈ [Λ_{i−1}, Λ_i] the height w_ℝ sweeps from ∓1 to ±(2λ(x_i)−1), which equals ±1 only if λ(x_i) = 1; since the weights sum to 1 over 2N ≥ 2 pieces, w_{X,M} is discontinuous at every Λ_i, so it is not a continuous curve and the displayed substitution in the proof is invalid (the proof implicitly uses w_ℝ = (−1)^i(2(s−Λ_{i−1})/λ(x_i)−1)). Moreover def:weightset allows arbitrary real weights, and for negative weights the Λ_i are not increasing, so the parametrization is not even well defined; the theorem needs λ > 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct eq:weightconst to w_ℝ(s) = (−1)^i(2(s−Λ_{i−1})/λ(x_i)−1) and add the hypothesis λ > 0 (or treat signed weights separately).
issues.overall_effect: The central construction of Section 2 is malformed as printed, so thm:weightconst (and the constructions used in thm:weight and thm:weightstrength) do not define valid curves until the formula is repaired.
issues.title: eq:weightconst parametrization is discontinuous as written
issues.why_classification: The normalization by λ(x_i) and the positivity hypothesis are local, forced repairs that make the construction well defined and the proof's substitution valid; nothing else changes (for d = 2).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: whose preimages $h^{-1}(s)$ we equip with the standard spherical measure $\sigma$ normalized so that $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$
constructed as in Section \ref{sec:weight} is a weighted $t$-design curve on $S^d$ of length greater than or equal to $\pi|X|$

issues.failure_explanation: The identity (1/2)∫_{−1}^{1}∫_{h^{−1}(s)} f dσ ds = ∫_{S^d} f dσ, with σ the normalized slice measure, holds only for d = 2. By the coarea formula ∫_{S^d} f dσ = c_d ∫_{−1}^{1} (1−s²)^{(d−2)/2} ∫_{h^{−1}(s)} f dσ ds with c_d = |S^{d−1}|/|S^d|. Hence for d ≥ 3 (and d = 1) the uniform-in-height parametrization does not reproduce the spherical measure: e.g. d = 3, X = {±e₁,±e₂,±e₃} ⊂ S² with equal weights 1/6 (a weighted 2-design set) and any M gives ∫₀¹ x₁(w_{X,M}(s))² ds = 1/3 ≠ 1/4 = ∫_{S³} x₁² dσ. So w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve for d ≥ 3, t ≥ 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reparametrize the height sweep on each piece with density proportional to (1−z²)^{(d−2)/2} (the image and length of each meridian piece are unchanged) and replace the proof's identity by the correct coarea formula; all stated length and design conclusions then hold for every d.
issues.overall_effect: The general-d proof of thm:weight is invalid for d ≥ 4 (the d = 3 case has its own route) and thm:weightstrength fails for d ≠ 2; the abstract's claim of the weighted result for all d ∈ ℕ₊ is unsupported as proven.
issues.title: thm:weightconst is false for d ≠ 2 (wrong coarea factor)
issues.why_classification: The construction as stated is false in a wide regime, but a contained repair (a reparametrized construction plus the correct coarea identity) preserves every theorem, bound, and advertised regime; no global proof architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For n = 0 the sphere is S¹. A simple closed geodesic cycle on S¹ is a simple traversal of the whole circle, so its normalized arc-length measure equals σ and ε_t = 0 exactly for every t; hence no sequence of simple ε_t-approximate t-design cycles on S¹ satisfies ε_t ≍ 1/t, and the theorem is false at n = 0. The proof also breaks there: Y_t ⊂ CP⁰ is a single point, W_t = 0, and thm:const's hypothesis range (0, (|Y|−1)sup d] = (0,0] is empty.

failure_location.quote: there exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of simple $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design cycles on $S^{2n+1}$ satisfying $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{2n}$ and $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$ as $t\to\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict thm:main to n ≥ 1 (or treat S¹ separately, noting the honest error is ε_t = 0), and give thm:even's n = 1 case a separate input or argument.
issues.overall_effect: The n = 0 endpoint of thm:main (i.e. d = 1, claimed in the abstract) is false as stated, and the derivation of thm:even for n = 1, which feeds on thm:main at n = 0, is broken.
issues.title: thm:main fails in the degenerate case n = 0
issues.why_classification: Excluding the degenerate endpoint n = 0 is a local hypothesis change that preserves the theorem's content for all n ≥ 1; only a vacuous/benign endpoint is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Three defects: (i) Proposition pro:covrad concerns D_t = sup_{y₁} inf_{y₂≠y₁} d(y₁,y₂), a separation radius, not the covering radius ρ_t, so 'ρ_t ≍ 1/t' is not supplied by the cited result; (ii) even granting a covering radius ρ_t, every MST edge has length ≤ 2ρ_t (midpoint argument), so W_t ≤ 4(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t — the stated bound with factor 1/4 is numerically false for well-distributed optimal-size design sets, where typical edge ≈ spacing ≈ ρ_t gives W_t ≈ 2|Y_t|ρ_t; (iii) the two-sided claim ε_t ≍ 1_t requires the never-established lower bound W_t ≳ t^{2n−1} (only W_t ≲ t^{2n−1} is argued).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the needed estimates: covering radius ρ_t ≲ 1/t for the design sets (standard design-implies-covering argument), the MST bound W_t ≤ 4(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t, and a lower bound W_t ≳ t^{2n−1} for the chosen sets — or weaken the conclusion to ε_t ≲ 1/t.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative conclusion ε_t ≷ 1/t of thm:main (and the same claim inherited by thm:even) is not established by the proof as written; the length order ℓ ≍ t^{2n} survives with corrected constants.
issues.title: Unjustified W_t estimates in the proof of thm:main
issues.why_classification: The proof's final quantitative step is invalid as written and needs a contained but nontrivial added argument (or a limited weakening from ≍ to ≲), while the main existence and length results survive.

issues.failure_explanation: At n = 0 the target is S⁰ = {±1}: every continuous closed curve in S⁰ is constant, has length 0 (so ℓ(γ_t) ≍ t^{−3} is impossible) and has approximation error bounded below by a positive constant (so ε_t ≍ 1/t is impossible). The stated derivation via pro:caps also requires d ≥ 2, so the n = 0 case is neither true nor derived.

failure_location.quote: there exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of simple $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves on $S^{2n}$ satisfying $\varepsilon_t\asymp 1/t$ and $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{4n-3}$ as $t\to\infty$

issues.overall_effect: The n = 0 endpoint of thm:even (the sphere S⁰) is false as stated; the content for n ≥ 1 is unaffected.
issues.title: thm:even fails in the degenerate case n = 0
issues.why_classification: Excluding the vacuous endpoint n = 0 is a local hypothesis change with no mathematical loss for the intended even-dimensional spheres.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: take $S$ to be the (finite) set of $s\in[0,1]$ such that $\gamma(s)$ is not smooth

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is internally inconsistent: S is finite, so ℓ(γ|_S) = 0 ≠ δ/2 (the intent is the open set S̃); 'S ⊂ γ(S)' is meaningless as written; and replacing a length-δ/2 piece of γ by a length-δ/2 piece of γ̃ leaves the length unchanged, contradicting the stated ℓ(γ̃) = ℓ(γ)+δ and error ε+2δc, which require replacing length δ/2 by 3δ/2. As given the proof establishes neither the length nor the error claim.

failure_location.quote: Consider an open subset $\widetilde S\subset[0,1]$ such that $\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$ and $S\subset\gamma(S)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the proof with consistent bookkeeping: modify γ on an open set S̃ with ℓ(γ|_{S̃}) = δ/2 so that the replacement piece has length 3δ/2, giving length change +δ and error at most 2δc, and fix the S/S̃ notation.
issues.overall_effect: lem:smooth (used to assert the smooth-curve variants of thm:const and thm:main) is unproven as written; its statement is plausible and routinely repairable.
issues.title: Internally inconsistent proof of lem:smooth
issues.why_classification: A local rewrite of a short proof with the intended constants restores the lemma; no construction, conclusion, or downstream guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality only separates consecutive children's anchor arcs; it does not prevent the last child's arc [δ_{d_{y,n_y}}, δ_{d_{y,n_y}}+δ̃] from overlapping the arrival arc [0, δ̃] of D_y when δ_{d_{y,n_y}} < δ̃, which the stated range [0, 2π/N_Y − δ̃) permits. Then the D_y are not pairwise disjoint, |⋃_y D_y| < 2(|Y|−1)δ̃ = δ, the claimed length identity fails, and Γ_Y acquires degree-1 vertices (anchors fall inside removed arcs), so it is not a union of closed curves and no simple closed curve covering it exists. Additionally, z_{d_{y,j}} = g_{z_y}(1)e^{i(…)} lies on the fiber over the parent y, not '∈ d_{y,j}', and g_{z_y} maps to S^{2n+1}, not S^3.

failure_location.quote: are pairwise disjoint for all $y\in Y\setminus\{y_0\}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the offsets (e.g. δ_{d_{y,j}} ∈ [δ̃, 2π/N_Y − δ̃)) or re-index so the last child's arc cannot overlap the arrival arc, and correct the fiber memberships and the ambient sphere S^{2n+1}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of lem:connecting (and hence the cited justification of thm:const's construction for arbitrary δ ∈ (0, M_Y)) is invalid as written; the lemma's existential statement is true for restricted parameter choices.
issues.title: Disjointness gap and misstatements in lem:connecting
issues.why_classification: A local restriction on already-free parameters plus two index corrections repair the construction; the lemma's statement and all downstream guarantees survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: these results can be verified from Remark \ref{rmk:hybrid} combined with the facts that the vertices of a tetrahedron and of an octahedron constitute 2 and 3-design sets respectively on $S^2$
the triple of the set $\{(0,0,-1)\}$, the curve $s\mapsto(2\sqrt{2}\cos s,2\sqrt{2}\sin s,1)/3$, and the balancing constant $1/4$ constitutes a hybrid 2-design

issues.failure_explanation: The weight adjustment ρ′ = ρ + 2π/ℓ(γ) does not make the two hybrid-design identities equivalent: matching the contributions of X, of the circle S^d∩P, and of the remaining curve requires ρ′/(|X|+s) = ρ/|X| and (1−ρ′)/ℓ(γ_P) = (1−ρ)/ℓ(γ) together with the polygon/circle exchange, which forces ρsℓ(γ) = 2π(1−ρ)|X| — not implied by the hypotheses. Counterexample: Ehler's hybrid 2-design ({(0,0,−1)}, latitude circle, 1/4) on S² with P the circle's plane (so γ_P is empty): the transformation outputs the tetrahedron vertex set with an empty curve and balancing constant 1/4 + 3/(2√2) > 1, which is not a hybrid design (already f ≡ 1 fails). The 'if and only if' is therefore false, and the claimed verifications via the remark are invalid.

failure_location.quote: $(X,\gamma,\rho)$ is a hybrid $t$-design if and only if $(X\cup X_P,\gamma_P,\rho+2\pi/\ell(\gamma))$ is a hybrid $t$-design.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rederive the transformation: state the correct output balancing constant together with the necessary input balancing condition (e.g. ρsℓ(γ) = 2π(1−ρ)|X|), and re-verify the tetrahedron/octahedron examples directly (they are independently true).
issues.overall_effect: The stated equivalence is false, and the paper's asserted verifications of Ehler's hybrid-design examples and of the subsequent generalized examples 'from Remark rmk:hybrid' are unsupported.
issues.title: rmk:hybrid transformation is false
issues.why_classification: The remark's claim is simply false and needs a rederived, hypothesis-laden replacement (a contained but nontrivial fix); the surrounding examples survive via direct verification, so the loss is limited.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as the vertices $\{v_i\}_{i=1}^{d+1}$ of a regular simplex constitute a 2-design set on $S^d$
and the balancing constant $1/4$ constitutes a hybrid 2-design

issues.failure_explanation: A regular simplex inscribed in S^d has d+2 vertices; {v_i}_{i=1}^{d+1} (d+1 vertices lying in an equatorial S^{d−1}) is not a 2-design on S^d, and the stated triple is not a hybrid 2-design: for d = 2 it reads (∅, circle, 0) — a pure single-circle 'design', which fails quadratic polynomials (Ehler's S² example has balancing constant 1/4 = 1−3/(d+2), not 0); for d = 3 the stated ({v₄}, circle, 1/4) gives 1/3 instead of the required 1/4 for f = ⟨x, v₄⟩². The prose claims a specific hybrid design that does not exist as described.

failure_location.quote: the triple of the set $\{v_i\}_{i=4}^{d+1}$, the curve $s\mapsto S^d$ which traces around the unique circle containing $\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}$, and the balancing constant $1-3/(d+1)$ constitutes a hybrid 2-design

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace d+1 by d+2 in the simplex size, the index range of the set, and the balancing constant (1−3/(d+2)), matching Ehler's d = 2 case.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted d-dimensional generalization of Ehler's simplex-based hybrid 2-design is false as written (for every d); the corrected version with d+2 vertices, set {v_i}_{i=4}^{d+2}, and constant 1−3/(d+2) is valid.
issues.title: Simplex hybrid-design example off by one (d+1 vs d+2 vertices)
issues.why_classification: A forced off-by-one correction (checked against the quoted ρ = 1/4 example at d = 2) restores the claim with no other change to any argument or scope.
